clue.text: Bird with bad back, a young one

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word bad from right to left

parts.note: a chick is a young bird

explanation.surface: A bird with a bad back, and a youngster at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BAD into DAB; a DABCHICK is the little grebe.
explanation.definitionFit: The dabchick is a small diving waterbird, the little grebe.

clue.text: Fold or go bust with red ace?

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of go, red and the ace are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A card player wonders whether to fold or go bust holding a red ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' looks like the poker move, but it is the corner turned down on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-ear is a page corner folded over, and to dog-ear is to fold one.

clue.text: Magistrates take note of test

parts.note: the bench is the collective term for magistrates sitting in court
to mark something is to take note of it

explanation.surface: Magistrates take note of a piece of evidence being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a standard reference point used to test performance.

clue.text: Undo knot after hot dog

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the H

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: to knot is to tangle, so the letters of undo are twisted together anew

explanation.surface: Instructions to undo a knot once something hot has been handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' at the end is the definition; 'Undo knot' reads as an instruction but 'knot' is the signal to tangle the preceding word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound is a hunting dog, and the word is used for dogs generally.

clue.text: Brownies, for example, as served with fresh cream

indicators.note: fresh suggests something newly made, so the letters of as and cream are remade

explanation.surface: Chocolate brownies served with fresh cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brownie was a famous range of cheap Kodak box cameras, not a chocolate cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Kodak Brownies were popular box cameras, so they are examples of the device.

clue.text: Beer is a big hit

definitions.meaning: in British slang beer or ale is called ...

explanation.surface: Beer packs quite a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallop is British slang for beer and also means a heavy blow.

clue.text: Shock with repeated exclamation while mounting horse

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: repeated means the exclamation appears twice in a row

parts.note: O is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means going upward, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as she spoke'

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in shock, over and over, while climbing onto a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns AS into SA; 'repeated' doubles the O.
explanation.definitionFit: The appaloosa is a North American horse breed with a spotted coat.

clue.text: Not bound to be promiscuous

explanation.surface: Someone untied and free to sleep around.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means untied or unfastened, and also sexually free or immoral.

clue.text: Unlawfully copying sanctimonious sailor

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
a rating is an ordinary sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: A self-righteous sailor caught making illegal copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirating means copying and selling material in breach of copyright.

clue.text: After drinks, may lose a game

indicators.note: after places the shortened word behind the two spirits

parts.note: gin and rum are two spirits

indicators.note: lose tells us to drop a letter, the one named by the following a

explanation.surface: After a few drinks, someone may well lose a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose a' takes A from MAY, leaving MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a two-player card game.

clue.text: Rumpus when boat enters old city

indicators.note: enters puts the boat inside the city's name

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
a proa is a Malay sailing boat

explanation.surface: Uproar breaks out when a boat sails into an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Uproar and rumpus both mean a noisy disturbance.

clue.text: Bull worshipped by Egyptians is under a Pharaoh initially

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the word below the other pieces
initially means only the opening letter of Pharaoh is used

explanation.surface: A sacred bull of the Egyptians is subject to a Pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: Apis was the sacred bull worshipped at Memphis in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Pest kept under wraps by a party leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: something kept under wraps is hidden

explanation.surface: A political pest is concealed by the party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are sap-sucking insects, a common garden pest.

clue.text: Feel remorse about measure that's obnoxious

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remorse word wraps around the measure

parts.note: to repent is to feel remorse
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a measure that proved obnoxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Repellent describes something offensive or disgusting, which is what obnoxious means.

clue.text: V-sign changes

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A rude V-sign changes things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V-sign' looks like the rude gesture, but it is V plus a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Varies is a verb meaning changes or alters.

clue.text: Monica's in trouble, having a problem getting off

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of Monica's and in are jumbled

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Monica is in trouble, unable to get off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting off' means getting off to sleep, not leaving a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to drop off to sleep is sleepless, which the adjective describes.

clue.text: German bread tax introduced by senator

indicators.note: a word introduced by another is placed inside it

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A senator brings in a tax on German bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a German fruit bread eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Going far from capital, don abandoned country house

indicators.note: abandoned tells us the following word is dropped from the capital's name

parts.note: London is the UK's capital
taken as written, the letters removed from the capital
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: Travelling far from the capital, a don abandons a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes DON from LONDON, leaving LON.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range describes something able to travel or reach a great distance.

clue.text: Two chaps showing signs of amusement

parts.note: Chuck is a man's name
Les is a man's name

explanation.surface: Two men are seen laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuckles are quiet laughs, which show amusement.

clue.text: Going round fine country, greeting artist

indicators.note: going round means the greeting surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: hi is a greeting
OK means fine
USA is a country

explanation.surface: An artist travels round a fine country, greeting people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokusai was the Japanese printmaker famous for The Great Wave off Kanagawa.

clue.text: One is covering head of Rupert Murdoch, she wrote

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: One is covering the head of Rupert Murdoch, the media tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rupert Murdoch' looks like the media tycoon; the definition is Murdoch the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was a British novelist and philosopher, author of The Sea, the Sea.

clue.text: Statement of grievance from one employed in factory

indicators.note: something employed in a place is working inside it

parts.note: a plant is a factory
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A complaint from a factory worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaint is a complaint or lament, especially a formal one in law.

clue.text: Quickly name an English city

parts.note: presto means quickly, in music

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to name an English city quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire in north-west England.

clue.text: Child upset by shoddy articles in arbitrary order

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a kid is a child
tat is cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: A child is upset by cheap junk issued under arbitrary rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a decree imposed without consent, an order given arbitrarily.

clue.text: Pantomime character having to join forces around Lake Superior

indicators.note: around means the joining word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to combine is to join forces
U stands for upper class, so superior

explanation.surface: A pantomime character teams up around Lake Superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Superior' looks like the Great Lake, but gives L and U. A pantomime is a British Christmas comedy show; Columbine is Harlequin's sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbine is the sweetheart of Harlequin in the harlequinade of pantomime.

clue.text: Primate runs after large bird

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the other pieces

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A primate runs after a big bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in Madagascar.

clue.text: Bones of sea dogs on island

parts.note: tars are sailors, old sea dogs

explanation.surface: Bones of old sailors found on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi are the bones of the ankle, plural of tarsus.

clue.text: Tent of tribal elder, possibly, easily erected at first

indicators.note: at first means the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A tribal elder's tent, perhaps, goes up easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent used by North American Plains peoples.

clue.text: After lacking firmness, I had to be quite clear

indicators.note: after places the contraction behind the slack word

parts.note: limp means slack, lacking firmness
I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: After going limp, someone makes things quite clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid means transparent or clear, of water or of prose.

clue.text: Nepotist about to get a move on

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of nepotist are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nepotist is about to hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom meaning hurry up, like pressing the accelerator.

clue.text: Uncompromising detective inspector has left the manor

indicators.note: has left tells us the officer departs from the area word

parts.note: in British police slang a manor is an officer's district or patch

explanation.surface: A tough detective inspector has quit his patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has left' takes DI out of DISTRICT. A manor is British police slang for the area a station covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict means rigid and unbending, so uncompromising.

clue.text: Order to besiege empty castle is offensive

indicators.note: to besiege is to surround, so the order goes round the castle's letters

parts.note: an indent is an official order for goods

indicators.note: empty means the inside of castle is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: An order to besiege an empty castle is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: An indent is a British term for an official requisition or order for supplies, which may be unfamiliar outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means offensive to accepted standards of decency.
